props.gloss_en: one should always pray in a house that has windows
as it is stated: 'and he had windows open in his upper chamber...' (Dan 6:11)
one might think a person may pray the whole day long; it is already explicit through Daniel [that it is three times]
'and three times [a day] he knelt upon his knees and prayed' (Dan 6:11)
one might think [Daniel's fixed prayer] began only when he came to the exile; [it is stated: he did so before]
it is already stated: 'as he had done before this' (Dan 6:11)
one might think a person may pray toward any direction he wishes; [the verse says: toward Jerusalem]
the verse says: 'toward Jerusalem' (Dan 6:11)
one might think he may include [the three prayers] all at once; it is already explicit through David [that they are evening, morning and noon]
as it is written: 'evening and morning and noon [I pray and cry aloud]' (Ps 55:18)
one might think he may make his voice heard in his prayer; it is already explicit through Hannah [that he may not]
as it is stated: 'and her voice was not heard' (I Sam 1:13)
one might think a person asks for his needs and afterwards prays; it is already explicit through Solomon [that prayer comes first]
as it is stated: 'to hearken to the song and to the prayer' (I Kings 8:28)
'song' (rina) is prayer
'prayer' (tefilla, in the verse) is request
one does not say a matter of request after emet veyatziv
but after the prayer, he may say even [requests] like the order of the Yom Kippur confession
[the Sages] said: a person asks for his needs in 'who hears prayer'
Rav: although they said one asks his needs in 'who hears prayer', if he comes to say [them] after his prayer, he may say even [requests] like the order of Yom Kippur
